extracted.intended_audience: researchers, university research administrators, and research groups seeking DFG coordinated programme funding
extracted.subtask_description: A concise overview of the DFG's coordinated funding instruments, describing the aims, typical duration, and emphases of each programme type to help applicants identify appropriate funding routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated Programmes — overall objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinated programmes promote cooperation and structural innovation by encouraging national and international collaboration in areas of current relevance and by concentrating scientific potential at a university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programmes are intended to foster collaborative structures and institutional strengthening at universities; suitability should be judged by potential for cooperation, structural innovation, relevance of topic, and concentration of scientific expertise at a host university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular feature of the Priority Programme is the nationwide collaboration between its participating researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority Programmes emphasize nationwide (Germany-wide) collaborative research across participating groups. Applicants should propose projects that clearly build on and coordinate with other groups nationwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Groups are established by universities to promote early career researchers. They are funded by the DFG for a period of up to nine years. Their key emphasis is on the qualification of doctoral researchers within the framework of a focused research programme and a structured training strategy. Research Training Groups with an interdisciplinary approach are warmly welcomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate a focused research programme, a structured doctoral training strategy, plans for qualifying PhD researchers, and may highlight interdisciplinary design; note the funding term limit of up to nine years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Research Centres
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative Research Centres are long-term university-based research institutions, established for up to 12 years, in which researchers work together within a multidisciplinary research programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable proposals are long-term, institutionally anchored, and multidisciplinary; applicants should plan multi-year, large-scale collaboration fitting the up-to-12-year funding horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFG Research Centres
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary objective of this programme is to establish a limited number of internationally visible and competitive research centres at German universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should aim to create internationally visible, competitive centre-level research structures at German universities; emphasis on visibility and competitiveness is central to selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Units
rubrics_metrics.description: A Research Unit is made up of a team of researchers working together on a research project which, in terms of thematic focus, duration and finances, extends beyond the funding options available under the Individual Grants Programme or Priority Programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Unit proposals should justify why the project exceeds scope/duration/finance limits of individual grants or priority programmes, demonstrating a shared team effort and a thematic focus requiring greater resources or time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Research Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Research Units provide outstanding researchers the opportunity to carry out close, medium-term cooperation in a special research project from the field of disease or patient-oriented clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for disease- or patient-oriented clinical research, applicants should present outstanding researcher teams and medium-term cooperative project plans focused on clinical relevance and patient-oriented outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centres for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Centres for Advanced Studies in the Humanities and Social Sciences are a special type of funding instrument specifically tailored to the working methods used in these particular fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals in humanities and social sciences should account for disciplinary working methods and justify the need for a tailored centre instrument; rationale should reflect field-specific practices and formats.
